newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa likely sell initial 49 pct of SAA.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa likely sell initial 49 pct of SAA.

text.p: The South Africa government would consider initially privatising up to 49 percent of national flag carrier South African Airways (SAA), Transport Minister Mac Maharaj said on Monday.
"I'm not sure we'll move for 100 percent. I think we might move again along the 49 percent route," he told Reuters after a news briefing.
Maharaj said labour groups had agreed, in principle, to a foreign strategic equity partner taking a stake in the national airline.
"There has also been important in principle agreement that we need to move fast," he added.
The government has previously announced plans to seek a minority equity partner in SAA during 1998 and fully privatise the carrier over several years.

Maharaj said in the case of SAA he would be prepared to relax laws prohibiting foreign ownership in a state carrier to 25 percent, as he had done with the ongoing privatisation of domestic airline Sun Air.
Companies to have already expressed an interest in SAA include British Airways Plc, Virgin Atlantic and Deutsche Lufthansa AG.
Maharaj said he saw few labour relations hurdles in moving to privatise SAA.
"Having reached the in principle agreement, we can move fast from here," he said.

He said other internal issues related to the unbundling of the Transnet parastatal, which included the apportioning to SAA of Transnet's total debt and pensions burden, would be resolved within a few months.
